verses.rationale: Keeps the administrative role and difficult geographic landmarks.
verses.before: Next to him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armory at the Angle.
verses.after: Beside him Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section opposite the ascent to the armory at the Angle.

verses.before: After him Baruch son of Zabbai zealously repaired another section, from the Angle to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest.
verses.after: After him Baruch son of Zaccai worked zealously on another section, from the Angle to the entrance of the house of Eliashib the high priest.

verses.rationale: Retains the repeated builder with full lineage and precise house boundaries.

verses.after: After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the entrance of Eliashib’s house to the end of the house.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired another section, from the door of Eliashib’s house to the end of Eliashib’s house.

verses.rationale: Preserves the priests’ regional association without fixing a disputed location.
verses.before: After him the priests, men from the surrounding district, repaired.
verses.after: After him the priests from the surrounding plain made repairs.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him the priests, men from the surrounding district, repaired.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two household locations and full ancestry.
verses.before: After them Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their house. After them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, repaired beside his house.
verses.after: After them Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their house. After them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, repaired beside his house.
verses.tsw_comparator: After them Benjamin and Hasshub repaired opposite their house. After them Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, repaired beside his house.

verses.rationale: Retains both named landmarks without collapsing angle and corner.
verses.before: After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from Azariah’s house to the Angle and to the corner.
verses.after: After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from Azariah’s house to the Angle and the Corner.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him Binnui son of Henadad repaired another section, from Azariah’s house to the Angle and to the corner.

verses.rationale: Supplies the implied repair verb while retaining the palace/tower attachment and next worker.
verses.before: Palal son of Uzai repaired opposite the Angle and the tower projecting from the upper house of the king, by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh repaired.
verses.after: Palal son of Uzai repaired opposite the Angle and the projecting tower of the upper royal house, by the court of the guard. After him came Pedaiah son of Parosh.
verses.tsw_comparator: Palal son of Uzai repaired opposite the Angle and the tower projecting from the upper house of the king, by the court of the guard. After him Pedaiah son of Parosh repaired.

verses.rationale: Preserves this settlement notice within the building register without adding an unstated work verb.
verses.before: The temple servants were living on Ophel as far as the place opposite the Water Gate toward the east and the projecting tower.
verses.after: The temple servants lived on the Ophel, as far as the area opposite the Water Gate on the east and the projecting tower.
verses.tsw_comparator: The temple servants were living on Ophel as far as the place opposite the Water Gate toward the east and the projecting tower.

verses.rationale: Keeps the Tekoites’ second contribution and its endpoints.
verses.before: After him the Tekoites repaired another section, opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of Ophel.
verses.after: After him the men of Tekoa repaired another section, from opposite the great projecting tower to the wall of the Ophel.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him the Tekoites repaired another section, opposite the great projecting tower as far as the wall of Ophel.

verses.rationale: Retains the location and distributed household work.
verses.before: Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each opposite his own house.
verses.after: Above the Horse Gate, the priests made repairs, each opposite his own house.
verses.tsw_comparator: Above the Horse Gate the priests repaired, each opposite his own house.

verses.rationale: Keeps Zadok’s house and Shemaiah’s gatekeeping office distinct.
verses.before: After them Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate, repaired.
verses.after: After them Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his house. After him came Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate.
verses.tsw_comparator: After them Zadok son of Immer repaired opposite his house. After him Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, keeper of the East Gate, repaired.

verses.rationale: Follows the read after him and retains the sixth-son designation and small dwelling.
verses.before: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his chamber.
verses.after: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After them Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his room.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, repaired another section. After him Meshullam son of Berechiah repaired opposite his chamber.

verses.rationale: Follows the read after him and preserves occupational and geographic details.
verses.before: After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the temple servants and merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate and as far as the upper room at the corner.
verses.after: After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the temple servants and merchants, opposite the Muster Gate, and as far as the upper room at the Corner.
verses.tsw_comparator: After him Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, repaired as far as the house of the temple servants and merchants, opposite the Inspection Gate and as far as the upper room at the corner.

verses.rationale: Closes the circuit at the starting gate and retains both working groups.
verses.before: Between the upper room at the corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants repaired.
verses.after: Between the upper room at the Corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants made repairs.
verses.tsw_comparator: Between the upper room at the corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants repaired.

verses.rationale: Maps Hebrew 3:33 to public 4:1 and preserves the first-person narrator’s return.
verses.before: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he became angry and very indignant, and he mocked the Jews.
verses.after: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he became furious. He mocked the Jews
verses.tsw_comparator: When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he became angry and very indignant, and he mocked the Jews.

verses.rationale: Keeps all mocking questions and the life-from-rubble image; uncertain first question noted.
verses.before: He said before his relatives and the army of Samaria, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive stones from heaps of rubble, stones that have been burned?”
verses.after: before his associates and the army of Samaria: “What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring stones back to life from these heaps of rubble—burned stones?”
verses.tsw_comparator: He said before his relatives and the army of Samaria, “What are these feeble Jews doing? Will they restore it for themselves? Will they sacrifice? Will they finish in a day? Will they revive stones from heaps of rubble, stones that have been burned?”

verses.rationale: Preserves the fox image and the second speaker’s sneer.
verses.before: Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him and said, “Even what they are building—if a fox climbed on it, it would break down their stone wall!”
verses.after: Tobiah the Ammonite, standing beside him, added, “Even a fox climbing on what they are building would break down their stone wall!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him and said, “Even what they are building—if a fox climbed on it, it would break down their stone wall!”

verses.rationale: Keeps the severe retaliatory prayer in the narrator’s voice without softening it.
verses.before: “Hear, our God, for we are despised. Turn their reproach back upon their own heads, and give them as plunder in a land of captivity.
verses.after: Hear us, our God, for we are despised! Turn their insults back on their own heads. Hand them over as plunder in a land of captivity.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Hear, our God, for we are despised. Turn their reproach back upon their own heads, and give them as plunder in a land of captivity.

verses.rationale: Retains the requested nonforgiveness and notes the implied object of provocation.
verses.before: Do not cover their guilt, and do not let their sin be blotted out before you, for they have provoked you before the builders.”
verses.after: Do not cover their wrongdoing or wipe their sin away from your sight, for they have provoked you in front of the builders.
verses.tsw_comparator: Do not cover their guilt, and do not let their sin be blotted out before you, for they have provoked you before the builders.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both the physical progress and heart-based resolve.
verses.before: So we built the wall, and the whole wall was joined together to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.
verses.after: So we rebuilt the wall, joining it all together up to half its height. The people had their hearts in the work.
verses.tsw_comparator: So we built the wall, and the whole wall was joined together to half its height, for the people had a heart to work.

verses.rationale: Maps original 4:1 to public 4:7, retaining every opposing group and repair progress.
verses.before: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of Jerusalem’s walls was advancing and that the breaches were beginning to be closed, they became very angry.
verses.after: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that Jerusalem’s walls were being repaired and the gaps were beginning to close, they became very angry.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the Ashdodites heard that the repair of Jerusalem’s walls was advancing and that the breaches were beginning to be closed, they became very angry.

verses.rationale: Keeps the coordinated attack and disruption purpose.
verses.before: All of them conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and create confusion in it.
verses.after: They all plotted together to come and fight against Jerusalem and throw it into confusion.
verses.tsw_comparator: All of them conspired together to come and fight against Jerusalem and create confusion in it.

verses.rationale: Retains prayer and practical defense side by side.
verses.before: But we prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night because of them.
verses.after: We prayed to our God and posted a guard against them day and night.
verses.tsw_comparator: But we prayed to our God and set a guard against them day and night because of them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the rhythmic complaint as lines within the verse paragraph.
verses.before: Judah said, “The strength of the burden-bearers is failing, and there is much rubble. We are not able to rebuild the wall.”
verses.after: Then the people of Judah said, “The carriers’ strength is failing, and there is so much rubble. We cannot build the wall.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Judah said, “The strength of the burden-bearers is failing, and there is much rubble. We are not able to rebuild the wall.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the planned surprise and killing explicit in enemy speech.
verses.before: Our adversaries said, “They will not know or see until we come among them, kill them, and stop the work.”
verses.after: Our enemies said, “They will not know or see us until we are among them. Then we will kill them and stop the work.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Our adversaries said, “They will not know or see until we come among them, kill them, and stop the work.”

verses.rationale: Retains the difficult return wording and tenfold warning rather than replacing it with an unmarked enemy-attack paraphrase.
verses.before: When the Jews who lived near them came, they said to us ten times, “From every place you turn, they will come against us.”
verses.after: The Jews who lived near them came and told us ten times, “You must return to us from every place.”
verses.tsw_comparator: When the Jews who lived near them came, they said to us ten times, “From every place you turn, they will come against us.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the family arrangement, vulnerable locations, and all weapons.
verses.before: So I stationed people in the lowest places behind the wall, in the exposed places. I stationed the people by families with their swords, spears, and bows.
verses.after: So I stationed people by families in the low, exposed places behind the wall, with their swords, spears, and bows.
verses.tsw_comparator: So I stationed people in the lowest places behind the wall, in the exposed places. I stationed the people by families with their swords, spears, and bows.

verses.rationale: Preserves the call to remember and every relationship at risk.
verses.before: I looked and arose and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, great and awe-inspiring, and fight for your relatives, your sons and daughters, your wives, and your houses.”
verses.after: After looking things over, I stood up and told the nobles, officials, and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the great and awe-inspiring Lord, and fight for your brothers, sons, daughters, wives, and homes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I looked and arose and said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, great and awe-inspiring, and fight for your relatives, your sons and daughters, your wives, and your houses.”

verses.rationale: Keeps divine frustration and the individual return to work.
verses.before: When our enemies heard that their plan was known to us, and God had frustrated their counsel, all of us returned to the wall, each to the work.
verses.after: When our enemies heard that their plan was known to us and that God had frustrated it, we all returned to the wall, each to his work.
verses.tsw_comparator: When our enemies heard that their plan was known to us, and God had frustrated their counsel, all of us returned to the wall, each to the work.

verses.rationale: Preserves the half-and-half arrangement and the leaders’ support at the sentence boundary.
verses.before: From that day, half of my servants worked on the construction and half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The leaders stood behind the whole house of Judah.
verses.after: From that day on, half my men worked while the other half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The leaders stood behind all the people of Judah
verses.tsw_comparator: From that day, half of my servants worked on the construction and half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The leaders stood behind the whole house of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinction between builders and load carriers and the one-hand image.
verses.before: Those building the wall and those carrying burdens worked with one hand doing the work and the other holding a weapon.
verses.after: who were building the wall. Those carrying loads worked with one hand and held a weapon with the other.
verses.tsw_comparator: Those building the wall and those carrying burdens worked with one hand doing the work and the other holding a weapon.

verses.rationale: Retains the builders’ equipment and signaler’s proximity to Nehemiah.
verses.before: Each builder had a sword strapped at the side while building, and the one who sounded the trumpet stayed beside me.
verses.after: Each builder worked with his sword strapped at his side. The man who sounded the ram’s horn stayed beside me.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each builder had a sword strapped at the side while building, and the one who sounded the trumpet stayed beside me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the practical problem of distance and dispersed labor.
verses.before: I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “The work is great and spread out, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.
verses.after: I told the nobles, officials, and the rest of the people, “The work is spread over a wide area, and we are far apart along the wall.
verses.tsw_comparator: I said to the nobles, the officials, and the rest of the people, “The work is great and spread out, and we are separated on the wall, far from one another.

verses.rationale: Keeps the gathering instruction and Nehemiah’s assurance together.
verses.before: Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, gather there to us. Our God will fight for us.”
verses.after: Wherever you hear the ram’s horn, gather to us there. Our God will fight for us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Wherever you hear the sound of the trumpet, gather there to us. Our God will fight for us.”

verses.rationale: Retains the long workday’s natural-light boundaries and guard proportion.
verses.before: So we worked at the work, while half held the spears from the rising of dawn until the stars came out.
verses.after: We kept working, with half the men holding spears, from daybreak until the stars appeared.
verses.tsw_comparator: So we worked at the work, while half held the spears from the rising of dawn until the stars came out.

verses.rationale: Keeps the servant relationship and the two duties without erasing the labor burden.
verses.before: At that time I also said to the people, “Let each person and servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and labor by day.”
verses.after: At that time I also told the people, “Each man and his servant must spend the night inside Jerusalem, so they can guard us by night and work by day.”
verses.tsw_comparator: At that time I also said to the people, “Let each person and servant spend the night inside Jerusalem, so that they may be a guard for us by night and labor by day.”

verses.rationale: Preserves continual readiness and offers a contextual rendering of the difficult final water clause, with uncertainty noted.
verses.before: Neither I, nor my relatives, nor my servants, nor the men of the guard who followed me took off our clothes; each kept a weapon at hand, even at the water.
verses.after: Neither I, my brothers, my men, nor the guards who followed me took off our clothes. Each kept his weapon even when going for water.
verses.tsw_comparator: Neither I, nor my relatives, nor my servants, nor the men of the guard who followed me took off our clothes; each kept a weapon at hand, even at the water.

verses.rationale: Keeps wives’ participation in the complaint explicit and preserves its internal communal target.
verses.before: There was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.
verses.after: A great outcry arose from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.
verses.tsw_comparator: There was a great outcry from the people and their wives against their fellow Jews.

verses.rationale: Retains the family needs and immediate survival appeal.
verses.before: Some were saying, “We, our sons, and our daughters are many. We need grain so that we may eat and live.”
verses.after: Some said, “There are many of us, with our sons and daughters. We need grain so we can eat and stay alive.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Some were saying, “We, our sons, and our daughters are many. We need grain so that we may eat and live.”

verses.rationale: Preserves all three pledged assets and the famine’s pressure.
verses.before: Others were saying, “We are pledging our fields, vineyards, and houses so that we may get grain during the famine.”
verses.after: Others said, “We are mortgaging our fields, vineyards, and houses to get grain during the famine.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Others were saying, “We are pledging our fields, vineyards, and houses so that we may get grain during the famine.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the tax-driven borrowing and collateral distinct from famine borrowing.
verses.before: Others were saying, “We have borrowed money for the king’s tax on our fields and vineyards.
verses.after: Still others said, “We have borrowed silver against our fields and vineyards to pay the king’s tax.
verses.tsw_comparator: Others were saying, “We have borrowed money for the king’s tax on our fields and vineyards.

verses.rationale: Retains the shared-flesh appeal, daughters’ particular harm, enslavement, and loss of land.
verses.before: Now our flesh is like the flesh of our relatives, our children like their children. Yet we are bringing our sons and daughters into servitude, and some of our daughters are already enslaved. We are powerless, because our fields and vineyards belong to others.”
verses.after: Our flesh is like our brothers’ flesh, and our children are like their children. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery. Some of our daughters are already enslaved, and we are powerless: our fields and vineyards belong to others.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Now our flesh is like the flesh of our relatives, our children like their children. Yet we are bringing our sons and daughters into servitude, and some of our daughters are already enslaved. We are powerless, because our fields and vineyards belong to others.”

verses.rationale: Keeps the narrator’s strong emotional response tied to what was heard.
verses.before: I became very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.
verses.after: I was very angry when I heard their outcry and these reports.
verses.tsw_comparator: I became very angry when I heard their outcry and these words.

verses.rationale: Unfolds the heart’s deliberation and retains public confrontation; the disputed debt term is noted.
verses.before: I considered the matter within myself and contended with the nobles and officials. I said to them, “Each of you is charging interest to your own relatives.” Then I held a great assembly against them.
verses.after: After thinking it through, I confronted the nobles and officials. “You are charging interest to your own brothers!” I told them. Then I called a large assembly against them.
verses.tsw_comparator: I considered the matter within myself and contended with the nobles and officials. I said to them, “Each of you is charging interest to your own relatives.” Then I held a great assembly against them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the repeated buying and selling and the creditors’ silence.
verses.before: I said to them, “As far as we were able, we bought back our fellow Jews who had been sold to the nations. And now you are selling your own relatives so that they may be sold back to us?” They were silent and could not find a word.
verses.after: I said, “As far as we could, we have bought back our fellow Jews who were sold to the nations. Now you are selling your own brothers, so they must be sold back to us!” They fell silent and could find nothing to say.
verses.tsw_comparator: I said to them, “As far as we were able, we bought back our fellow Jews who had been sold to the nations. And now you are selling your own relatives so that they may be sold back to us?” They were silent and could not find a word.

verses.rationale: Follows the read first-person said and keeps the walk/fear language and concern about reproach.
verses.before: So I said, “What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?
verses.after: I went on, “What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, to avoid the insults of the nations who are our enemies?
verses.tsw_comparator: So I said, “What you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?

verses.rationale: Includes Nehemiah’s own circle and preserves the inclusive demand to relinquish the charge.
verses.before: I also, along with my relatives and servants, have been lending them money and grain. Please, let us leave off this interest.
verses.after: I, my brothers, and my men are also lending them silver and grain. Let us stop charging this interest.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also, along with my relatives and servants, have been lending them money and grain. Please, let us leave off this interest.

verses.rationale: Keeps every asset and commodity and the stated hundredth without assigning an unstated period.
verses.before: Restore to them today their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses, along with the hundredth part of the money, grain, new wine, and oil that you have been charging them.”
verses.after: Give back their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses today, along with the hundredth part of the silver, grain, new wine, and oil that you are charging them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Restore to them today their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses, along with the hundredth part of the money, grain, new wine, and oil that you have been charging them.”

verses.rationale: Identifies who swears while retaining priests as witnesses and the full restitution pledge.
verses.before: They said, “We will restore it and require nothing from them. We will do as you say.” Then I called the priests and made them swear to do according to this word.
verses.after: They answered, “We will give it back and demand nothing from them. We will do as you say.” I summoned the priests and made the creditors swear to carry out this promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: They said, “We will restore it and require nothing from them. We will do as you say.” Then I called the priests and made them swear to do according to this word.

verses.rationale: Preserves the acted curse, repeated shaking, public assent, and reported compliance.
verses.before: I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, “So may God shake out from house and possession everyone who does not fulfill this word. So may that person be shaken out and emptied.” All the assembly said, “Amen,” and praised the LORD. And the people did according to this word.
verses.after: I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, “May God shake out of his house and his possessions everyone who fails to keep this promise. May he be shaken out and left empty like this!” The whole assembly said, “Amen,” and praised the LORD. The people kept their promise.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, “So may God shake out from house and possession everyone who does not fulfill this word. So may that person be shaken out and emptied.” All the assembly said, “Amen,” and praised the LORD. And the people did according to this word.

verses.rationale: Keeps the retrospective twelve-year span and the relinquished allowance.
verses.before: Moreover, from the day I was appointed governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes—twelve years—I and my relatives did not eat the governor’s food allowance.
verses.after: From the day I was appointed governor in Judah—from the twentieth to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years—neither I nor my brothers ate the governor’s food allowance.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moreover, from the day I was appointed governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes—twelve years—I and my relatives did not eat the governor’s food allowance.

verses.rationale: Preserves the amount without inventing a daily frequency and keeps servants’ abuse explicit.
verses.before: The former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them bread and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their servants ruled harshly over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.
verses.after: The earlier governors had burdened the people, taking food and wine from them, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their servants lorded it over the people. I did not act that way, because I feared God.
verses.tsw_comparator: The former governors who were before me laid heavy burdens on the people and took from them bread and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their servants ruled harshly over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.

verses.rationale: Keeps labor and refusal to acquire land in the same self-account.
verses.before: I also devoted myself to the work on this wall, and we acquired no land. All my servants were gathered there for the work.
verses.after: I also devoted myself to work on this wall. We acquired no fields, and all my men were gathered there for the work.
verses.tsw_comparator: I also devoted myself to the work on this wall, and we acquired no land. All my servants were gathered there for the work.

verses.rationale: Preserves the base guest count and additional visitors.
verses.before: At my table were one hundred fifty Jews and officials, besides people who came to us from the nations around us.
verses.after: At my table were 150 Jews and officials, besides those who came to us from the surrounding nations.

verses.tsw_comparator: You divided the sea before them, and they passed through the midst of the sea on dry ground; but you threw their pursuers into the depths, like a stone into mighty waters.

verses.rationale: Retains both guiding pillars and day/night parallelism.
verses.before: By a pillar of cloud you led them by day, and by a pillar of fire at night, to give them light on the way in which they should go.
verses.after: By a pillar of cloud you led them by day, and by a pillar of fire at night, to light the way they should go.
verses.tsw_comparator: By a pillar of cloud you led them by day, and by a pillar of fire at night, to give them light on the way in which they should go.

verses.rationale: Preserves both locations and the differentiated instruction categories.
verses.before: You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them right judgments, true teachings, good statutes and commandments.
verses.after: You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them just judgments, trustworthy instructions, and good statutes and commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke with them from heaven. You gave them right judgments, true teachings, good statutes and commandments.

verses.rationale: Keeps Sabbath’s holiness and Mosaic mediation.
verses.before: You revealed to them your holy Sabbath and commanded them commandments, statutes, and Torah through Moses your servant.
verses.after: You made your holy Sabbath known to them and gave them commands, statutes, and instruction through your servant Moses.
verses.tsw_comparator: You made known to them your holy Sabbath and commanded them commandments, statutes, and Torah through Moses your servant.

verses.rationale: Preserves paired hunger/thirst provision and the raised-hand oath image.
verses.before: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and brought water from the rock for their thirst. You told them to go in and possess the land that you had raised your hand to give them.
verses.after: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and brought water from a rock for their thirst. You told them to enter and possess the land you had raised your hand in oath to give them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You gave them bread from heaven for their hunger and brought water from the rock for their thirst. You told them to go in and possess the land that you had raised your hand to give them.

verses.rationale: Retains the ancestral identification and bodily resistance image.
verses.before: But they and our ancestors acted arrogantly, stiffened their necks, and did not listen to your commandments.
verses.after: But they, our ancestors, acted arrogantly. They stiffened their necks and did not listen to your commands.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they and our ancestors acted arrogantly, stiffened their necks, and did not listen to your commandments.

verses.rationale: Keeps the source’s in their rebellion rather than substituting Egypt and preserves the extended divine character refrain.
verses.before: They refused to listen and did not remember your wonders that you had done among them. They stiffened their necks and, in their rebellion, appointed a leader to return to their slavery. But you are a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love, and you did not abandon them.
verses.after: They refused to listen and did not remember the wonders you had done among them. They stiffened their necks and appointed a leader to return to slavery in their rebellion. But you are a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and rich in faithful love. You did not abandon them.
verses.tsw_comparator: They refused to listen and did not remember your wonders that you had done among them. They stiffened their necks and, in their rebellion, appointed a leader to return to their slavery. But you are a God of forgiveness, gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in steadfast love, and you did not abandon them.

verses.rationale: Preserves the singular calf claim and suspended sentence leading to compassion.
verses.before: Even when they made for themselves a cast calf and said, ‘This is your God who brought you up from Egypt,’ and committed great acts of contempt,
verses.after: Even when they made themselves a cast-metal calf and said, ‘This is your God who brought you up from Egypt,’ and committed great blasphemies,
verses.tsw_comparator: Even when they made for themselves a cast calf and said, ‘This is your God who brought you up from Egypt,’ and committed great acts of contempt,

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated nonabandonment and both guiding images rather than condensing the retelling.
verses.before: you, in your great mercies, did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from above them by day to lead them on the way, nor the pillar of fire by night to give them light on the way they should go.
verses.after: you, in your great compassion, did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not leave them by day, to guide them on the way, nor the pillar of fire by night, to light the way they should go.
verses.tsw_comparator: you, in your great mercies, did not abandon them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud did not depart from above them by day to lead them on the way, nor the pillar of fire by night to give them light on the way they should go.

verses.rationale: Retains Spirit, instruction, manna, mouths, and thirst as distinct gifts.
verses.before: You gave your good Spirit to instruct them, did not withhold your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst.
verses.after: You gave your good Spirit to instruct them. You did not withhold your manna from their mouths, and you gave them water for their thirst.
verses.tsw_comparator: You gave your good Spirit to instruct them, did not withhold your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst.

verses.rationale: Preserves the duration and specific bodily and material provisions.
verses.before: Forty years you sustained them in the wilderness; they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
verses.after: For forty years you sustained them in the wilderness. They lacked nothing; their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.
verses.tsw_comparator: Forty years you sustained them in the wilderness; they lacked nothing. Their clothes did not wear out, and their feet did not swell.

verses.rationale: Makes the difficult territorial clause readable while preserving the two named rulers and Heshbon relation.
verses.before: You gave them kingdoms and peoples and allotted them boundary by boundary. They possessed the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
verses.after: You gave them kingdoms and peoples, allotting them territory. They took possession of Sihon’s land, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.
verses.tsw_comparator: You gave them kingdoms and peoples and allotted them boundary by boundary. They possessed the land of Sihon, the land of the king of Heshbon, and the land of Og king of Bashan.

verses.rationale: Retains the star image and generational promise.
verses.before: You multiplied their children like the stars of heaven and brought them into the land that you had told their ancestors to enter and possess.
verses.after: You made their children as numerous as the stars of heaven and brought them into the land you had told their ancestors to enter and possess.
verses.tsw_comparator: You multiplied their children like the stars of heaven and brought them into the land that you had told their ancestors to enter and possess.

verses.rationale: Preserves conquest, subjection, and the conquerors’ broad power without softening harm.
verses.before: So their children entered and possessed the land. You subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand, along with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them according to their will.
verses.after: Their children entered and possessed the land. You subdued its inhabitants, the Canaanites, before them and handed over their kings and the peoples of the land for them to do with as they pleased.
verses.tsw_comparator: So their children entered and possessed the land. You subdued before them the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites, and gave them into their hand, along with their kings and the peoples of the land, to do with them according to their will.

verses.rationale: Retains the complete acquired-resource list and bodily abundance image.
verses.before: They captured fortified cities and a rich land and possessed houses filled with every good thing, cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. They ate, were satisfied, grew fat, and delighted in your great goodness.
verses.after: They captured fortified cities and fertile land, houses full of good things, cisterns already cut, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. They ate, were satisfied, and grew fat, delighting in your great goodness.
verses.tsw_comparator: They captured fortified cities and a rich land and possessed houses filled with every good thing, cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and fruit trees in abundance. They ate, were satisfied, grew fat, and delighted in your great goodness.

verses.rationale: Preserves defiance, the back image, prophet killing, and repeated blasphemy.
verses.before: Yet they rebelled and acted defiantly against you. They threw your Torah behind their backs and killed your prophets who warned them in order to turn them back to you, and they committed great acts of contempt.
verses.after: But they defied you and rebelled against you. They threw your instruction behind their backs and killed your prophets, who warned them to return to you. They committed great blasphemies.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet they rebelled and acted defiantly against you. They threw your Torah behind their backs and killed your prophets who warned them in order to turn them back to you, and they committed great acts of contempt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the oppression–cry–hearing–deliverance pattern and hand image.
verses.before: So you gave them into the hand of their adversaries, who oppressed them. In the time of their distress they cried to you, and you heard from heaven. According to your great mercies, you gave them deliverers who delivered them from the hand of their adversaries.
verses.after: So you handed them over to their enemies, who oppressed them. In their distress they cried to you, and you heard from heaven. In your great compassion you gave them deliverers who saved them from their enemies’ hands.
verses.tsw_comparator: So you gave them into the hand of their adversaries, who oppressed them. In the time of their distress they cried to you, and you heard from heaven. According to your great mercies, you gave them deliverers who delivered them from the hand of their adversaries.

verses.rationale: Retains repetition as the prayer’s organizing pattern rather than treating it as redundant.
verses.before: But when they had rest, they again did evil before you. So you abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, who ruled over them. Yet when they returned and cried to you, you heard from heaven, and according to your mercies you delivered them many times.
verses.after: But as soon as they had rest, they did evil before you again. You abandoned them into their enemies’ hands, and their enemies ruled over them. Again they cried to you, and you heard from heaven. Time after time you rescued them in your compassion.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when they had rest, they again did evil before you. So you abandoned them into the hand of their enemies, who ruled over them. Yet when they returned and cried to you, you heard from heaven, and according to your mercies you delivered them many times.

verses.rationale: Preserves the life statement and both bodily resistance images.
verses.before: You warned them in order to turn them back to your Torah, but they acted arrogantly and did not listen to your commandments. They sinned against your judgments, by which a person who does them will live. They turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks, and would not listen.
verses.after: You warned them to return to your instruction, but they acted arrogantly and did not listen to your commands. They sinned against your judgments, which give life to the person who does them. They turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks, and would not listen.
verses.tsw_comparator: You warned them in order to turn them back to your Torah, but they acted arrogantly and did not listen to your commandments. They sinned against your judgments, by which a person who does them shall live. They turned a stubborn shoulder, stiffened their necks, and would not listen.

verses.rationale: Keeps patience, Spirit-mediated warning, refusal, and consequence.
verses.before: You were patient with them for many years and warned them by your Spirit through your prophets, but they would not give ear. So you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.
verses.after: For many years you were patient with them. By your Spirit you warned them through your prophets, but they would not listen. So you handed them over to the peoples of the lands.
verses.tsw_comparator: You were patient with them for many years and warned them by your Spirit through your prophets, but they would not give ear. So you gave them into the hand of the peoples of the lands.

verses.rationale: Preserves both restrained destruction and nonabandonment within the recurring refrain.
verses.before: Yet in your great mercies you did not make an end of them or abandon them, for you are a gracious and compassionate God.
verses.after: Yet in your great compassion you did not finish them off or abandon them, for you are a gracious and compassionate God.
verses.tsw_comparator: Yet in your great mercies you did not make an end of them or abandon them, for you are a gracious and compassionate God.

verses.rationale: Keeps the appeal, six affected groups, and historical span.
verses.before: Now therefore, our God—the great, mighty, and awe-inspiring God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love—do not let all the hardship seem small before you that has come upon us, our kings, our officials, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.
verses.after: Now, our God, great, mighty, and awe-inspiring God, you keep covenant and faithful love. Do not regard as small all the hardship that has come upon us— our kings, officials, priests, prophets, ancestors, and all your people— from the days of Assyria’s kings until today.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now therefore, our God—the great, mighty, and awe-inspiring God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love—do not let all the hardship seem small before you that has come upon us, our kings, our officials, our priests, our prophets, our ancestors, and all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until this day.

verses.rationale: Preserves the prayer’s contrast of divine faithfulness and communal guilt.
verses.before: You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for you have acted faithfully, but we have acted wickedly.
verses.after: You have been righteous in all that has come upon us. You have acted faithfully; we have done wrong.
verses.tsw_comparator: You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for you have acted faithfully, but we have acted wickedly.

verses.rationale: Keeps the named leadership groups and two neglected forms of address.
verses.before: Our kings, officials, priests, and ancestors did not keep your Torah or pay attention to your commandments and your warnings by which you warned them.
verses.after: Our kings, officials, priests, and ancestors did not carry out your instruction. They did not attend to your commands or the warnings you gave them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Our kings, officials, priests, and ancestors did not keep your Torah or pay attention to your commandments and your warnings by which you warned them.

verses.rationale: Retains the favorable conditions and failure to serve and turn.
verses.before: Even in their kingdom, and in your great goodness that you gave them, and in the broad and rich land you set before them, they did not serve you or turn from their evil deeds.
verses.after: Even in their own kingdom, amid the great goodness you gave them and the broad, fertile land you set before them, they did not serve you or turn from their evil deeds.
verses.tsw_comparator: Even in their kingdom, and in your great goodness that you gave them, and in the broad and rich land you set before them, they did not serve you or turn from their evil deeds.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated slavery and the bitter location contrast rather than rendering political subjection vaguely.
verses.before: Look, we are servants today. As for the land you gave to our ancestors to eat its fruit and its good things—look, we are servants in it.
verses.after: Look at us today: we are slaves! In the land you gave our ancestors to eat its fruit and its good things— here we are, slaves in it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Look, we are servants today. As for the land you gave to our ancestors to eat its fruit and its good things—look, we are servants in it.

verses.rationale: Preserves external control of produce, bodies, and animals and the prayer’s unresolved distress.
verses.before: Its abundant produce goes to the kings you have set over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and our livestock according to their pleasure, and we are in great distress.
verses.after: Its rich produce goes to the kings you have set over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and our livestock as they please. We are in great distress.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Its abundant produce goes to the kings you have set over us because of our sins. They rule over our bodies and our livestock according to their pleasure, and we are in great distress.

verses.rationale: Binds original 10:1 to public 9:38 and retains the written agreement and sealing groups.
verses.before: Because of all this, we make a firm agreement in writing, and our officials, Levites, and priests put their seals upon it.”
verses.after: Because of all this, we are making a firm agreement and putting it in writing. Our officials, Levites, and priests place their seals on it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of all this, we make a firm agreement in writing, and our officials, Levites, and priests put their seals upon it.”

verses.rationale: Maps original 10:2 and introduces the sealed signatories with the narrator’s title and father.
verses.before: People who sealed it were Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah;
verses.after: Those who sealed it were Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah;
verses.tsw_comparator: Those who sealed it were Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah;

verses.rationale: Preserves the first three priestly signatories in order.
verses.before: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah;
verses.after: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah;

verses.rationale: Keeps each name in the continuing signatory list.
verses.before: Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah;
verses.after: Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah;

verses.rationale: Retains these three priestly names without identifying namesakes.
verses.before: Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch;
verses.after: Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch;

verses.rationale: Preserves the complete three-name sequence.
verses.before: Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah;
verses.after: Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah;

verses.rationale: Keeps all three names and the source’s Ginnethon form.
verses.before: Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch;
verses.after: Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
verses.tsw_comparator: Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch;

verses.rationale: Retains all three signatories in order.
verses.before: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin;
verses.after: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
verses.tsw_comparator: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin;

verses.rationale: Preserves the concluding three names and retrospective priestly identification.
verses.before: Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
verses.after: Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
verses.tsw_comparator: Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.

verses.rationale: Keeps the two different genealogical qualifications.
verses.before: The Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the descendants of Henadad, and Kadmiel;
verses.after: The Levites were Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the family of Henadad, Kadmiel,
verses.tsw_comparator: The Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from the descendants of Henadad, and Kadmiel;

verses.rationale: Retains the kinship grouping and all five names.
verses.before: and their relatives Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan;
verses.after: and their relatives Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan,
verses.tsw_comparator: and their relatives Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan;

verses.rationale: Preserves the three Levite names in order.
verses.before: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah;
verses.after: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah;

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated Shebaniah as a separate occurrence.
verses.before: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah;
verses.after: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah;

verses.before: Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
verses.after: Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.

verses.rationale: Marks the new group and preserves all five names.
verses.before: The heads of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani;
verses.after: The heads of the people were Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani,
verses.tsw_comparator: The heads of the people: Parosh, Pahath-moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani;

verses.rationale: Keeps Bunni distinct from the preceding Bani and preserves all names.
verses.before: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai;
verses.after: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
verses.tsw_comparator: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai;

verses.rationale: Retains the three named heads of the people.
verses.before: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin;
verses.after: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
verses.tsw_comparator: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin;

verses.rationale: Preserves Hezekiah as a separate name rather than importing a family relation from the register.
verses.before: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur;
verses.after: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
verses.tsw_comparator: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur;

verses.rationale: Keeps these three names in the source’s sequence.
verses.before: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai;
verses.after: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai;

verses.rationale: Follows the read Nebai rather than written Nobai.
verses.before: Hariph, Anathoth, Nobai;
verses.after: Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hariph, Anathoth, Nobai;

verses.rationale: Retains all three names without shortening the list.
verses.before: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir;
verses.after: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
verses.tsw_comparator: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir;

verses.rationale: Keeps the distinct signatories and their order.
verses.before: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua;
verses.after: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
verses.tsw_comparator: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua;

verses.rationale: Preserves the three names and repeated Hanan.
verses.before: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah;
verses.after: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah;

verses.rationale: Retains these three heads of the people.
verses.before: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub;
verses.after: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub;

verses.rationale: Keeps each of the three names intact.
verses.before: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek;
verses.after: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
verses.tsw_comparator: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek;

verses.rationale: Preserves Hashabnah’s form here and the surrounding names.
verses.before: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah;
verses.after: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
verses.tsw_comparator: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah;

verses.rationale: Keeps Hanan and Anan as separate similar-sounding names.
verses.before: Ahiah, Hanan, Anan;
verses.after: Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
verses.tsw_comparator: Ahiah, Hanan, Anan;

verses.rationale: Closes the signatory list with all three names.
verses.before: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.
verses.after: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

verses.rationale: Preserves every group, women and children, and the understanding qualification across the sentence.
verses.before: The rest of the people—the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and everyone who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the Torah of God, along with their wives, sons, and daughters, everyone with knowledge and understanding—
verses.after: The rest of the people—the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and everyone who had separated from the peoples of the lands to follow God’s instruction, with their wives, sons, and daughters, all who could know and understand—
verses.tsw_comparator: The rest of the people—the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and all who had separated themselves from the peoples of the lands to the Torah of God, along with their wives, sons, and daughters, everyone with knowledge and understanding—

verses.rationale: Keeps the self-binding curse, oath, walking image, and full instruction categories.
verses.before: joined with their relatives, their nobles, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the Torah of God given through Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, along with his judgments and statutes.
verses.after: joined their noble brothers in a curse and an oath: to walk in God’s instruction given through Moses, God’s servant, and to keep and carry out all the commands, judgments, and statutes of the LORD our Lord.
verses.tsw_comparator: joined with their relatives, their nobles, and entered into a curse and an oath to walk in the Torah of God given through Moses the servant of God, and to observe and do all the commandments of the LORD our Lord, along with his judgments and statutes.

verses.rationale: Retains both directions of the marriage commitment in the community’s own words.
verses.before: We would not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters for our sons.
verses.after: “We will not give our daughters in marriage to the peoples of the land or take their daughters for our sons.
verses.tsw_comparator: We would not give our daughters to the peoples of the land or take their daughters for our sons.

verses.rationale: Preserves trade restrictions and the seventh-year release, making the implied land-rest object explicit.
verses.before: If the peoples of the land bring merchandise or any grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day. We will also let the seventh year rest and release every debt.
verses.after: If the peoples of the land bring merchandise or any grain to sell on the Sabbath, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or a holy day. In the seventh year we will let the land rest and release every debt.
verses.tsw_comparator: If the peoples of the land bring merchandise or any grain to sell on the Sabbath day, we will not buy from them on the Sabbath or on a holy day. We will also let the seventh year rest and release every debt.

verses.rationale: Keeps the exact one-third amount without harmonizing the half-shekel elsewhere.
verses.before: We also placed ourselves under an obligation to give one-third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of our God:
verses.after: We accept the obligation to give a third of a shekel each year for the service of our God’s house:
verses.tsw_comparator: We also placed ourselves under an obligation to give one-third of a shekel each year for the service of the house of our God:

verses.rationale: Retains the full funding inventory and atonement purpose.
verses.before: for the bread of the Presence, the regular grain offering, the regular burnt offering, the Sabbaths, new moons, appointed festivals, holy things, sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.
verses.after: for the bread set out in rows, the regular grain offering and burnt offering, the Sabbaths, new moons, appointed festivals, holy offerings, sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of our God’s house.
verses.tsw_comparator: for the bread of the Presence, the regular grain offering, the regular burnt offering, the Sabbaths, new moons, appointed festivals, holy things, sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of the house of our God.

verses.rationale: Keeps all participants, the lot, recurring schedule, and altar purpose.
verses.before: We—the priests, Levites, and people—cast lots concerning the wood offering, to bring it to the house of our God by ancestral houses at appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as written in the Torah.
verses.after: We—the priests, Levites, and people—have cast lots by ancestral house for the wood offering, to bring it to our God’s house at appointed times each year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as written in the instruction.
verses.tsw_comparator: We—the priests, Levites, and people—cast lots concerning the wood offering, to bring it to the house of our God by ancestral houses at appointed times year by year, to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as written in the Torah.

verses.rationale: Preserves both agricultural categories and annual repetition.

verses.after: Was it not through marriages like these that Solomon king of Israel sinned? Among the many nations there was no king like him. His God loved him and made him king over all Israel, yet foreign wives led even him into sin.
verses.tsw_comparator: Did not Solomon king of Israel sin because of these things? Among many nations there was no king like him, and he was loved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Yet foreign women caused even him to sin.

verses.rationale: Retains the rhetorical question and attribution of unfaithfulness without extending it to a modern rule.
verses.before: Are we then to hear that you are doing all this great evil, acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?”
verses.after: Must we now hear that you too are doing all this great evil, being unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Are we then to hear that you are doing all this great evil, acting unfaithfully against our God by marrying foreign women?”

verses.rationale: Keeps the three-generation relationship and personal expulsion.
verses.before: One of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite, so I drove him away from me.
verses.after: One of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was Sanballat the Horonite’s son-in-law. I drove him away from me.
verses.tsw_comparator: One of the sons of Joiada son of Eliashib the high priest was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite, so I drove him away from me.

verses.rationale: Preserves the accusatory remember appeal and both covenant-related groups.
verses.before: Remember them, my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
verses.after: Remember them, my God, for defiling the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
verses.tsw_comparator: Remember them, my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.
